source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes jointly Gaussian additive disturbances and gives necessary-and-sufficient access conditions for identifying average outcomes E[Y|do(W)] using hard intervention distributions that leave each treatment free while intervening on its parents or a superset.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1 abstract; pp. 2–3, shift-intervention definitions and Section 3.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper distinguishes shifts defined with respect to natural treatment values (SITs) from recursively defined shift policies (SIPs), gives sound and complete identification algorithms, and studies a special mean-response estimator.

The paper introduces σ-calculus and proves its algorithm and calculus sound for identification and z-identification of general conditional and stochastic interventions from available observational and experimental distributions.

source_verification_receipts.version: NeurIPS 2015 proceedings, BACKSHIFT: Learning causal cyclic graphs from unknown shift interventions
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: BACKSHIFT studies linear cyclic models with latent variables under shift interventions and gives a necessary-and-sufficient identifiability condition based on covariance differences across environments.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Repair the inverse and intervention-domain definitions: state continuous versions of all conditional means, make f^D conditional on C_Δ=1, and impose an explicit almost-sure recursive K-domain condition for each target do-value.

Add BackShift2015 and CausalDantzig2019 to the related-work map, with a concise table separating noise-distribution shifts, natural-value shifts, linear versus nonlinear mechanisms, and structure versus full-law targets.

Turn the stability OEQ into a specified statistical experiment by naming a metric on regime laws, an operator norm or modulus, a finite-sample loss, and the local class over which its minimax converse ranges.

recommended_next_step: Revise the inverse/domain and stability definitions, then re-review the field-tier rank-cover theorem against an expanded shift-intervention literature map.
